<h3 align="center">Mock any Go HTTP client with the calls it really made.</h3>

Package cassette records HTTP calls as interactions, stored as JSON, and replays
them. One `http.RoundTripper`, `cassette.Replay`, does both: it mocks a client in
tests and records its real traffic, so there is no need to write one of your own.

## Introduction

A cassette is an `interactions.json` file: a list of requests, each with the
response it got. Hand it to `cassette.Replay` and any client that takes an
`*http.Client` gets those responses, without touching the network.

The package depends on nothing but the standard library and
[jsonutil](https://github.com/MarkRosemaker/jsonutil), so a library can depend
on it, and offer it to its users, at no cost.

## Features

- **Mock** a client in tests with `cassette.Replay(ias)`: each request is
  answered from the recording it matches, by method, URL with its query in any
  order, and body, compared as JSON. Any other request fails with
  `cassette.ErrNoInteraction`, without touching the network.
- **Record** with `cassette.Replay(ias, cassette.RecordMisses(nil))`: a request
  without a recording is sent and recorded, and `Recorder.Interactions` holds
  every call, ready for `Interactions.WriteFile`.
- **Test strictly** with `cassette.InOrder()` and `cassette.CompareHeaders(...)`:
  every call must match the next recording, headers included, and
  `Recorder.Unused` tells which recordings were never called.
- **Masking**: writing a file always masks credentials first, in headers, bodies
  and query values, as `Interactions.Mask` does.
- **Once per call**: `AddInteraction` writes a call to a file only if it is not
  in it yet, so a failure that recurs is recorded once.
- **Large bodies**: a body that is not text is never read or written, only
  marked `bodyOmitted`, so a download streams to its caller as it is. A JSON
  string longer than 2,048 bytes, such as an image in base64, is cut to that.
- **Stable files**: query parameters are sorted by name, so a recording does not
  change with the order a client happens to send them in.

## Usage

Mock a client in a test:

```go
ias, err := cassette.InteractionsReadFile("testdata/interactions.json")
if err != nil {
	t.Fatal(err)
}

client := &http.Client{Transport: cassette.Replay(ias)}
```

A client generated by
[openapi-codegen](https://github.com/MarkRosemaker/openapi-codegen) takes it as
`WithHTTPClient(&http.Client{Transport: cassette.Replay(ias)})`.

Record what has no recording yet, and save it:

```go
rec := cassette.Replay(ias, cassette.RecordMisses(nil))
client := &http.Client{Transport: rec}

// … make the calls …

if err := rec.Interactions().WriteFile("testdata/interactions.json"); err != nil {
	return err
}
```

Check every call against its recording, in order and with its headers:

```go
rec := cassette.Replay(ias, cassette.InOrder(), cassette.WithMatcher(
	cassette.MatchRequest(cassette.CompareHeaders("User-Agent")),
))

t.Cleanup(func() {
	if unused := rec.Unused(); len(unused) > 0 {
		t.Errorf("%d recordings were never replayed", len(unused))
	}
})
```

The package examples run each of these.

## Where it comes from

cassette started inside
[openapi-enrich](https://github.com/MarkRosemaker/openapi-enrich), which turns
recorded traffic into an OpenAPI specification, and
[openapi-codegen](https://github.com/MarkRosemaker/openapi-codegen) generates
clients whose tests replay it. It moved into a module of its own so that those
clients, and anyone else, can record and replay without depending on either.
